analysis.title: Macro DeMark US Equity Alert
key_insights: Perl did not expect the 11/5 equities sell-off but does not think it ended the bull market. He keeps his 8,485 SPX target for next year and recommends not selling into weakness, saying risk/reward into year-end and beyond is heavily skewed to the topside.

Cross-asset damage was limited outside Japan (which he says to avoid) and South Korea. SX5E, Hang Seng and Australia held up, and Mexico and India rose. He reads this as de-risking rather than de-leveraging, so the sell-off was likely corrective within the broader advance.

SOX is at the epicentre of the de-risking. It registered a TD Combo 11 Count on 11/5, so a TD Combo 13 Buy signal is possible as soon as Monday's close (11/9). That would be the first daily TD Combo Buy since the market topped over the summer.

63.30% of SOX constituents are at or near a DeMark Buy. Both daily and weekly TD Propulsion downside targets were hit at the low on 11/5. Perl says a one-day fall to a confluence of daily and weekly TD Propulsion Exhaustion levels, or to a monthly level (as SPX did at last year's Liberation Day low), is commonly followed by a tradable rebound.
SOX daily upside TD Propulsion Level, which would relieve the immediate downside threat, is 9,938. Early signs of recovery are 9,264 and 9,530.

NDX is one day behind SOX, with a daily TD Combo 10 Count on 11/5. The SPW vs NDX ratio was a daily TD Combo 11 Count, so a Sell (13) is possible as soon as Monday's close. 16.83% of NDX names are at or near a Sell and 29.71% are at or near a Buy.
Hang Seng is described as a developing Wave 3 on daily, weekly and monthly charts.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is the centre of the de-risking, with a TD Combo 11 Count and 63.30% of constituents at or near a DeMark Buy. Perl expects a tradable rebound, and a Buy 13 signal is possible on 11/9.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Perl's target implies substantial upside from current levels and supports buying rather than selling the dip.
